recommendations.rationale: Terminal reach, sampled holding position, sampled holding speed and computation are separately scoped observations with coverage of one endpoint (update 34, t = 0.35 s), 6 window samples and 35 updates. Before any change, screen one positive tip-speed weight (holding_tip_speed_weight or terminal_tip_speed_weight) in a bounded local comparison at a saved holding-window baseline update; treat the result as screening only, since a projected-model probe at or below 0.01 s effective horizon cannot explain the entire settling failure.

The retained evidence supports only temporal co-occurrence between the 35 deadline-missed updates (34 User_Requested_Stop versus 1 Solve_Succeeded, per-update wall times of order 17.57 s) and the holding-window excursions; it does not support a linkage beyond co-occurrence. Defer any causal claim or reconfiguration until a replay capability or full optimizer traces are available.

attribution.reason: reach_passed rides on the terminal endpoint error 0.007642608585867386 m, which is inside the 0.01 m tolerance, while the same final window contains up to 0.05813810428573256 m error and 0.6351726092425104-1.5810152739742807 m/s speed against the 0.01 m and 0.02 m/s limits. The terminal value is the window minimum for both error and speed, so the terminal pass is not representative of the window. Terminal reach, sampled holding position, sampled holding speed and computation are therefore best reported as co-occurring but independently scoped observations rather than as a single verdict.

The only relationship the retained evidence exhibits is temporal co-occurrence: 35 updates at a 0.01 s period with 34 User_Requested_Stop selections against 1 Solve_Succeeded and per-update wall times of order 17.57 s, alongside window excursions. Wall-clock overruns are synchronous and do not establish skipped simulated updates, no closed-loop counterfactual replay exists in this context, and full warm plans / optimizer iteration traces are not retained. A dominant cause cannot be established from one execution.

The retained configuration has holding_tip_speed_weight = 0.0 and terminal_tip_speed_weight = 0.0 with tip_speed_scale_m_s = 0.02, which is a testable contributor to a holding window whose sampled tip speeds (0.6351726092425104-1.5810152739742807 m/s) all exceed the 0.02 m/s settling limit. Raw weight magnitudes do not establish cost-term importance without actual contributions/scaling, and a bounded projected-model probe with effective horizon at or below 0.01 s cannot explain an entire settling failure, so this remains a bounded-exploration hypothesis, not proof of the dominant cause.

Recorded projection residuals (2.1832800954411686 rad/m at update 24, 2.7208545806103697 rad/m at update 33) and a predicted-versus-measured tip velocity difference norm of 0.10241202341919153 m/s (update 32) show that projected GVS states and serial-backend endpoints differ within the retained record, but nothing retained links that disagreement to the holding-window excursions, and closed-loop counterfactual replay is unavailable. The same limitation applies in the negative direction: the retained evidence neither establishes nor rules out a geometry or material contribution to settling or computation, and no geometry or material change is in scope.

facts.statement: Terminal reach passed at a single sampled endpoint: summary.reach_passed = true against reach_tolerance_m = 0.01 m, with terminal_error_m = 0.007642608585867386 m; the late-motion sample at the final recorded time carries the same 0.007642608585867386 m error. This flag is an endpoint observation (update 34, t = 0.35 s), not a whole-trajectory or whole-window statement.

Sampled holding position failed: holding_position_passed = false. The retained summary labels these as selected rows only, not whole-trajectory ranges or causal evidence.

Sampled holding speed failed: holding_speed_passed = false and sampled_settling_passed = false. Over the same 6 window samples tip speed ranges from 0.6351726092425104 m/s to 1.5810152739742807 m/s against the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit, with terminal tip speed 0.6351726092425104 m/s, i.e. the window minimum equals the terminal value and every sampled window speed exceeds the limit. The retained configuration records holding_tip_speed_weight = 0.0, terminal_tip_speed_weight = 0.0 and tip_speed_scale_m_s = 0.02; these are raw weight magnitudes without retained cost-term contribution or scaling data.

The retained per-update record contains 35 updates at control_period_s = 0.01 s, stopping counts Solve_Succeeded = 1 versus User_Requested_Stop = 34, full_snapshots_available = false, and per-update wall times of order 17.57 s (update 27) as recorded. Projected-model indicators are also recorded: projection residuals of 2.1832800954411686 rad/m (update 24) and 2.7208545806103697 rad/m (update 33), and an aligned-interval predicted-versus-measured tip velocity difference norm of 0.10241202341919153 m/s (update 32). These are observations of the retained record; synchronous wall overruns do not establish skipped or delayed simulated updates.

limitations: Selected samples only: the holding summaries cover the 6 recorded samples of the final 0.05 s window (t = 0.3-0.35 s), and terminal reach is one endpoint (update 34, t = 0.35 s); neither is a whole-trajectory range. Mid-trajectory motion is available only as matched prediction endpoints, not as a continuous series.

No causal identification: no closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal attribution tool is available in this context, and full warm plans and optimizer iteration traces (control_snapshots.json) are not retained; a single execution and model comparisons do not establish a dominant cause.

The combined flag joint_reach_holding_passed = false and the mean per-update wall time are stated in the request but are not backed by selected catalog handles here; only per-criterion flags and the listed per-update timings were selected. Per-update deadline-miss counts are likewise reported in the request rather than as selected handles.
Synchronous wall-clock deadline behaviour cannot be linked to the holding-window position/speed excursions beyond temporal co-occurrence, and lacks evidence of skipped or delayed simulated updates.
Raw weight magnitudes (holding_tip_speed_weight = 0.0, terminal_tip_speed_weight = 0.0) do not establish cost-term importance without retained contribution or scaling data, which is not available.

A bounded projected-model probe with effective horizon at or below 0.01 s is known to be insufficient to explain an entire settling failure and is not the basis of this report. Only terminal_tip_speed_weight and holding_tip_speed_weight are in scope for any later change; no geometry or material change is in scope.
recommended_actions: Defer any parameter change until a bounded local comparison at a saved holding-window baseline update screens one changed positive tip-speed weight (holding_tip_speed_weight or terminal_tip_speed_weight), reported as a screening result rather than as a fix; an inconclusive screen does not prohibit a later justified complete experiment.

Do not retune on temporal co-occurrence alone: the computation-versus-settling question requires a replay capability (closed-loop counterfactual replay or complete backend replay) and control_snapshots.json, neither of which is available in this phase.
